paragraphs: Blackburn is the larger of the two towns in the borough of Blackburn with Darwen, so children in care from the town are looked after by Blackburn with Darwen Council's own fostering service and by the agencies shown above.

Enquiries to the council now go through Foster with Us, a recruitment hub shared by five councils in the North West: Blackburn with Darwen, Blackpool, Lancashire County, Cumberland, and Westmorland and Furness. The hub answers questions seven days a week. It launched Foster Care Fortnight in May 2025 together with the Blackburn with Darwen fostering service, with the aim of finding 16 more foster carers in the borough that year.

The hub asks that carers are over 21 and have a spare room, unless they only care for babies, and that they have the right to work in the UK. In earlier appeals the council has said it most needs carers for children with complex emotional and physical needs, including parent and child placements, disabled children, step-down placements and young people on remand. It describes its allowances as depending on your skills and the child's age, with training, a social worker of your own, support groups and peer mentors for new carers.

Our Blackburn with Darwen page covers the whole borough, and our Lancashire, Blackpool and North West pages cover the wider area. Speak to the council through the hub and to two or three of the services above, and ask each what they pay, which children they most need homes for and how they support new carers.
